title: #stereophonic #stereophonicplay #stereophonicbroadway #stereophonicbw...
transcript: Last night, Paul and I saw Stereophonic on Broadway, easily one of the best new plays in New York right now. I saw this at Playwrights Horizons last fall and I loved it just as much the second time around. Following a 1970s rock band working on an album and how it affects their relationships, this is a sprawling three hour opus on the nature of music, creativity, ego, and collaboration. Everything about this piece is so beautifully specific: the writing, the characters, the set design, the costumes, the performances, the music that the actors play live — and this consistent specificity I think is what makes the play so captivating, as well as just getting to witness the creative spontaneity in these recording sessions. I would wholeheartedly recommend this play but I do wanna mention that some sightlines could be tricky from the rear mezz because of how deep the set is. There were a couple moments where we couldn't see some heads when the actors were very far upstage in the recording booth and I imagine the further back you are, the more this will happen, so I wouldn't recommend sitting much further back than where we were which is the front row of the rear mezz. And honestly of all the plays this season, I think this would be the one that warrants a splurge for a good seat. With that, another playbill for my collection.

The only caveat is about sightlines from the rear mezzanine, which is a practical note rather than a criticism of the production itself.
